text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا ۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِۦ ۚ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ

words.gloss_range: vocative particle opening a direct address that scopes the whole verdict scene
words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) gathers the two prisoners before any fate is distributed. The call turns the interpretation into face-to-face speech: after 12:40 speaks generally about people not knowing, this word narrows the scene to two addressed men. The ayah then moves from address, to the two partitioned outcomes, to a settled decree, with the long opening cadence separating the interpersonal summons from the terse legal-like apportionment that follows.

topics.headline: direct address scopes the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coming interpretation is not detached prediction but a directed verdict spoken to the two men.
topics.reason: Grammar and discourse rows agree that the vocative particle governs the dual address and frames the whole utterance as direct speech.

topics.headline: call-to-decree architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse narrowing from 12:40 general teaching into a complete addressed verdict scene.
topics.reason: The architecture rows trace address, partition, and decree, while the sound row supports the slowed opening before the fate clauses.

words.gloss_range: dual construct companion title; exactly two prison-defined addressees
words.root_gloss_range: companionship, association, and domain-holding root; here narrowed to two companions defined by confinement while custody or ownership pressure remains secondary
words.prose: {{ar:صَاحِبَيِ}} ({{tr:ṣāḥibay}}) names the addressees as a closed pair before the verse divides them. The dual construct makes companionship a present identity defined by prison, so the later one-and-other distribution is not generic. The same prison-companion address has just framed Joseph’s theological teaching in 12:39, and here it turns those same listeners into recipients of personal judgment. The broader {{ar:ص ح ب}} ({{tr:ṣ-ḥ-b}}) pattern of people defined by condition or environment, as in companion labels around fire, garden, or the whale (68:48; 2:81; 2:82), remains as provenance, but the local grammar selects these two prison companions.

topics.headline: exact two-person construct address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole verdict operates on a closed dyad, not an open group of prisoners.
topics.reason: The dual form, construct relation, and later dual verb all keep the same two addressees in view.

topics.headline: companionship defined by confinement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that companionship is a standing prison identity before the two fates split it apart.
topics.reason: The semantic rows preserve association, custody, and active-participle pressure, while local syntax narrows the sense to companions of the prison.

topics.headline: environment-defined companion formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prison dyad fits a wider Quranic habit of naming people by the environment or condition that defines them (68:48; 2:81; 2:82).
topics.reason: Intertextual rows compare environment-defined companion labels and the identical address in 12:39 without overriding the local vocative sense.

topics.headline: doctrine becomes addressed judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph turns from teaching the same companions in 12:39 to distributing their personal fates in 12:41.
topics.reason: Structural and boundary rows show the dual address seeding the later one-versus-other fate allocation.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive prison as the shared domain of the two addressees
words.root_gloss_range: confinement and imprisoning root; here a concrete known prison, with heavier judgment-register echoes kept secondary
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسِّجْنِ}} ({{tr:al-sijni}}) is grammatically dependent on the companion title but semantically dominates the scene. It makes confinement the shared domain from which one man moves toward service and the other toward public fixation and exposure. The {{ar:س ج ن}} ({{tr:s-j-n}}) root is narrowed to the concrete prison, while its rare Surah 12 concentration across Joseph’s confinement arc (12:33; 12:42; 12:100) and its heavier Sijjin-register neighbor (83:7-8) give the place more than background value. The boundary also matters: 12:40’s abstract judgment becomes embodied here in prison, service, crucifixion, birds, and a head, and 12:42 will keep the prison setting alive as delay.

topics.headline: known prison defines the pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prison is not scenery added later; it is the defining term of the address.
topics.reason: Case and construct evidence make the prison the genitive complement that specifies the two companions.

topics.headline: confinement escalates into exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from enclosed confinement to the second fate’s exposed bodily fixation.
topics.reason: Semantic and structure rows link the opening prison setting to service after prison and to the crucifixion-exposure branch.

topics.headline: rare prison root as surah-local thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prison term belongs to a repeated Surah 12 confinement-release arc (12:33; 12:42; 12:100), while the local sense remains a concrete jail.
topics.reason: Distribution and same-surah rows show concentration in Joseph’s prison narrative; cosmic ledger parallels are retained only as resonance, not as the local referent.

topics.headline: theological judgment becomes embodied scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that abstract judgment from 12:40 becomes visible in bodies, service, confinement, and delay.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the previous argument to the concrete prison scene and forward to continued confinement in 12:42.

words.gloss_range: first partition particle that topicalizes one member and requires an answering consequence
words.prose: {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) moves from the shared address into the first routed case. It is not complete by itself; it waits for the answering consequence particle and so turns one prisoner into a branch of a two-output verdict. The small compound form carries both topicalizing and conditional-distributive force.

topics.headline: first routed fate branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first fate is a branch inside a distribution, not an isolated prediction.
topics.reason: Grammar and structure rows agree that this particle opens a partition that must be answered by the following consequence marker.

words.gloss_range: one member selected from a dual addressee set while the identity remains withheld
words.root_gloss_range: oneness and singularity root; here ordinary partitive one-of-two, with divine uniqueness parallels kept as contrast only
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدُكُمَا}} ({{tr:aḥadukumā}}) fuses a singular one with a dual you, extracting one member from the addressed pair while not naming which man. That suspended identification lets the first branch become active service and sets up the definite other that follows; the one-other structure also resumes the dream report’s division in 12:36. The {{ar:أ ح د}} ({{tr:ʾ-ḥ-d}}) root’s absolute-uniqueness register is only contrastive here, including the contrast with divine oneness in 112:1; the local payoff is mortal one-of-two selection under a settled decree. Even the initial hamza gives the split an audible catch as the shared address breaks into individual fate assignment.

topics.headline: singular extracted from the dual pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word itself performs extraction: one member is selected from the two addressees.
topics.reason: The singular numeral and dual suffix jointly license a one-from-two reading and block collective interpretation.

topics.headline: first member of one-other verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the suspense of an ordered distribution: one receives service, the remaining other receives death-exposure, answering the one-other dream split in 12:36.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence and structure rows show the one-other pair controlling the verse’s two fates and echoing 12:36.

topics.headline: divine uniqueness register kept as contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a scale contrast between ordinary mortal individuation and the root’s better-known absolute uniqueness register in 112:1.
topics.reason: The semantic field includes divine uniqueness, but local grammar selects an unspecified mortal one from two.

topics.headline: sharp onset at the split
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audible and structural break from shared address into individual fate assignment.
topics.reason: Phonetic and echo rows reinforce the local split without adding a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: answering consequence particle fused to the first service verb
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) completes the first partition and pivots the named topic into an outcome. Because it is fused to the service verb, the logic of consequence is not postponed; the selected prisoner immediately receives his action as the first branch’s verdict.

topics.headline: first branch consequence hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the first topic becomes an enacted outcome through a tiny attached hinge.
topics.reason: The rows agree that the particle answers the first partition and is graphically bound to the service verb.

words.gloss_range: active imperfect service verb: the restored man gives drink to his master
words.root_gloss_range: watering and drink-provision root; here narrowed from general watering to courtly wine-service with active agency
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْقِي}} ({{tr:yasqī}}) makes the first fate active and social: the selected man will give drink, with a master as recipient and wine as the supplied drink. The {{ar:س ق ي}} ({{tr:s-q-y}}) field of watering is narrowed into court service, so survival is not simple freedom but restored hierarchy. Variant pressures expose direct service, mediated causation, and passive role inversion, but the surface reading keeps the servant personally performing the service. The drink-giving field also reverses scenes where a lord gives or receives provision differently (28:24; 76:21), and it anticipates the later Surah 12 cup motif at 12:70.

topics.headline: active service with recipient and drink
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surviving man is restored to an active service role, not merely spared.
topics.reason: Attachment and grammar evidence identify the hidden subject, recipient object, and drink object of the active imperfect.

topics.headline: variant spectrum tests agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that alternate readings highlight the agency spectrum, while the local surface preserves direct service.
topics.reason: Accepted variant rows can clarify role inversion or causative agency, but they do not replace the canonical active verb in this output.

topics.headline: life-watering redirected to wine service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ordinary watering field redirected into human courtly wine-service.
topics.reason: Lexical and distribution rows preserve the watering background while the local object narrows the action to wine service.

topics.headline: drink-giving echoes and cup motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this cup-bearing fate joins broader drink-giving scenes (28:24; 76:21) and the later Surah 12 cup motif at 12:70.
topics.reason: Intertextual rows compare divine and human drink-giving scenes (28:24; 76:21) and later same-surah cup language at 12:70 without changing the local verb sense.

words.gloss_range: possessed human master as recipient of the cupbearer’s service
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, mastery, ownership, and nurture root; here a human master selected by suffix and service context, with divine-dominant usage pressing by contrast
words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّهُ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) names the authority figure as the recipient of service, and the suffix makes him this servant’s master. The {{ar:ر ب ب}} ({{tr:r-b-b}}) root is locally human, not divine, yet its dominant lordship register makes the contrast sharp: visible earthly authority receives wine while the final decree belongs to a hidden higher authority, unlike explicit divine decreeing with the Lord in 17:23. Variant case and dotting rows sharpen the same point by testing whether grammar focuses on the master as the person served, a passive recipient-subject, or the state of quenching itself. Across the boundary, 12:40’s worship-and-judgment language becomes earthly service here, and 12:42 will make this human master relation the route of appeal.

topics.headline: possessed master receives service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first fate restores a personal master-servant relation, not generic employment.
topics.reason: Case, suffix, and valency evidence place the human master as recipient object of the service verb.

topics.headline: divine-loaded noun used for human master
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pressure created when a theologically dominant lordship word is locally steered toward a human master, in contrast with explicit divine decree language such as 17:23.
topics.reason: Lexical distribution supports the divine-dominant pressure, while the suffix and service context narrow the local referent to a human master.

topics.headline: case and dotting variants test beneficiary structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant evidence probes whether the focus is the master as person or the state of being quenched.
topics.reason: Variant rows clarify possible grammatical promotion or replacement, but the canonical local surface keeps the possessed master as object.

topics.headline: theological servitude becomes narrative service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary move from divine worship language in 12:40 to earthly service in 12:41, without equating the two.
topics.reason: Boundary and structure rows connect the human master relation to the prior theological frame and the next ayah’s appeal route.

words.gloss_range: indefinite concrete wine as the drink object completing the service frame
words.root_gloss_range: covering and wine/intoxicant root; here literal wine served to the master, with reason-veiling pressure retained as irony
words.prose: {{ar:خَمْرًا}} ({{tr:khamran}}) completes the first branch as the concrete substance of service. The accusative indefinite form names wine as the delivered object, not a vague circumstance or symbol. It also answers the earlier dream: wine pressed in 12:36 becomes wine served to the master in 12:41, while the paired bird image moves into the death branch. The {{ar:خ م ر}} ({{tr:kh-m-r}}) root’s covering and reason-veiling field remains active as irony: the substance that clouds judgment appears inside a verdict scene where the matter is clarified and decreed. Its rare Quranic wine register ranges through legal problem, prohibition, and paradise description (2:219; 5:90; 47:15), but here it remains literal service wine.

topics.headline: concrete second object of service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first fate closes on the actual service substance, not on abstract survival.
topics.reason: Grammar and form rows identify the accusative indefinite wine as the drink object in the two-object service frame.

topics.headline: reason-veiling substance inside clarified decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a cognition-veiling drink is served inside a scene of disclosed judgment.
topics.reason: Lexical rows preserve the covering/intoxicant pressure while the local noun remains literal wine.

topics.headline: dream wine becomes served wine
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the earlier dream image in 12:36 is fulfilled by being transformed from pressing wine into serving wine.
topics.reason: Same-surah echo rows tie the wine object to 12:36 and to the paired wine/bird dream field.

topics.headline: rare wine lexeme across legal and paradise registers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this literal service wine sits among sharply different Quranic wine registers (2:219; 5:90; 47:15).
topics.reason: Distribution and intertext rows mark rarity and cross-register movement, while the local function stays narrative service wine.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that joins the second partition to the first verdict branch
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) prevents the second fate from becoming a new speech act. It coordinates the second partition with the first, giving the two branches equal grammatical weight while the contents become radically unequal: service on one side, crucifixion and exposure on the other.

topics.headline: second branch coordinated with the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two opposite outcomes belong to one ordered disclosure.
topics.reason: The conjunction rows show both coordination and transition into the second case.

words.gloss_range: second partition particle mirroring the first while routing toward the fatal branch
words.prose: {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) repeats the partition frame and makes the second outcome formally parallel to the first before the content breaks symmetry. The listener hears a matched branch, then discovers that the matched form carries the opposite fate: passive execution and exposed aftermath.

topics.headline: parallel frame for unequal fate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how repetition creates formal balance while preparing a starkly unequal outcome.
topics.reason: The second partition requires its answering consequence and completes the bipartite distribution begun by the first partition.

words.gloss_range: definite remaining member of the pair, grammatically subject but semantically patient
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, lateness, and afterness root; here narrowed to the other prisoner, with death-facing afterlife resonance retained as secondary pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْءَاخَرُ}} ({{tr:al-ākharu}}) closes the pair: once one member has been routed to service, the definite other is the remaining man, just as the other dreamer was separated in 12:36. He receives subject position, but the passive verb that follows makes him a patient rather than an actor. The {{ar:أ خ ر}} ({{tr:ʾ-kh-r}}) field is locally otherness, while laterness and afterlife echoes press because this second branch becomes the death branch; Surah 12 itself has nearby afterlife uses of the same field (12:37; 12:101).

topics.headline: remaining member of the closed pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second man is not an additional outsider but the remaining member of the addressed two.
topics.reason: Definiteness and comparative form close the two-person set opened by the earlier one-of-you wording.

topics.headline: subject position without agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical tension: the other is subject on the surface but victim in the event.
topics.reason: Case and passive-predicate evidence make the other the grammatical subject of an imposed fate.

topics.headline: otherness with death-facing afterness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ordinary word for other carries afterness pressure in a branch that leads to death, against nearby afterlife uses in 12:37 and 12:101.
topics.reason: The root’s afterlife field is not the local denotation, but death-branch context licenses a narrowed resonance.

topics.headline: dream report returns in verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same one-other architecture from the dream report in 12:36 reappears as final apportionment.
topics.reason: Structure and same-surah rows link this word to the earlier dream split at 12:36.

words.gloss_range: answering consequence particle fused to the second passive fate
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) answers the second partition and turns the label “the other” into an imposed outcome. Its fusion with the passive execution verb makes crucifixion the immediate grammatical result of the second branch.

topics.headline: second branch consequence hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact pivot where classification becomes execution.
topics.reason: The particle is required by the second partition and is attached directly to the passive fate verb.

words.gloss_range: imperfect passive crucifixion: an imposed future execution with hidden human agent
words.root_gloss_range: crucifixion, rigidity, backbone, and cross/fixing field; here narrowed to public crucifixion as suffered fate
words.prose: {{ar:يُصْلَبُ}} ({{tr:yuṣlabu}}) makes the second man a passive victim of an imposed future event. The hidden executioner is kept offstage, while the outcome itself is foregrounded and then extended into bird-consumption. The {{ar:ص ل ب}} ({{tr:ṣ-l-b}}) field adds rigid bodily fixation and penal severity, and the stiff sound cluster matches that fixing, but the local sense is the public execution that enables the exposed aftermath. Its punishment register recalls Pharaoh threat scenes (7:124; 20:71; 26:49) and the legal punishment formula at 5:33, while the local passive keeps the focus on suffered fate rather than a tyrant’s boast.

topics.headline: imposed crucifixion with suppressed agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condemned man is grammatically acted upon, unlike the first man who acts in service.
topics.reason: Voice and attachment evidence suppress the human executioner and make the other prisoner the suffered subject.

topics.headline: rigid fixation and penal body field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete fixing of the body, not just a generic death prediction.
topics.reason: Root-family rows preserve rigidity, backbone, and cross-shape pressure while the local verb selects crucifixion.

topics.headline: rare punishment formula echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the juridical and tyrannical punishment register behind this compact prison verdict (7:124; 20:71; 26:49; 5:33).
topics.reason: Distribution and intertext rows compare Pharaoh-threat and legal-punishment formulas without making them the local speaker or procedure.

topics.headline: crucifixion enables bird consumption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that crucifixion is not the branch’s endpoint; it creates the condition for the exposed head scene.
topics.reason: Structure rows show the passive execution feeding the next consequence, and the voice-contrast row connects it to the larger pattern of service, imposed fate, and decree.

words.gloss_range: sequential consequence particle chaining bird-consumption to crucifixion
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) chains a second consequence onto the second fate. It makes the bird-eating scene dependent on crucifixion rather than an independent image, so the branch unfolds as an ordered cascade: execution, then exposed consumption.

topics.headline: second consequence in the death branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second fate unfolds in stages rather than stopping at execution.
topics.reason: The rows identify the particle as sequential and fused to the eating verb, linking the aftermath to crucifixion.

words.gloss_range: active imperfect eating by the collective birds, taking from the head as source
words.root_gloss_range: eating, consuming, and corroding root; here literal bird consumption from an exposed body part
words.prose: {{ar:تَأْكُلُ}} ({{tr:taʾkulu}}) shifts the branch from passive execution to active nonhuman consumption. The birds become the visible agents, while the prepositional phrase makes the head a source from which material is taken. The {{ar:أ ك ل}} ({{tr:ʾ-k-l}}) root is locally literal Form I eating, not an intensified or causative abstraction, with broader consuming or corroding pressure sharpening the image of irreversible bodily depletion. The wording recapitulates the bird-eating dream in 12:36 and sits within Surah 12’s animal-eating fatality motif at 12:17, while contrasting with life-sign bird scenes such as 3:49. The medial hamza gives the eating verb a small audible catch at the jarring turn into consumption.

topics.headline: active consumption after passive execution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the agency shift from hidden human executioner to visible birds acting on the exposed body.
topics.reason: Grammar and structure rows make the collective birds the subject of an active verbal clause after the passive crucifixion.

topics.headline: eating from a bodily source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the horror is partitive: the birds eat from the head, not simply a whole object called the head.
topics.reason: The governed prepositional complement shifts the verb from direct-object eating to source extraction.

topics.headline: literal eating with depletion pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices consumption as gradual, irreversible depletion while the local action remains literal bird eating.
topics.reason: Root-range rows add consuming and corroding pressure but do not abstract away from the concrete eating scene.

topics.headline: dream wording returns as interpretation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Joseph’s interpretation reactivating the earlier bird-eating dream language from 12:36 rather than paraphrasing it loosely.
topics.reason: Pairing and echo rows connect the eating-bird unit to 12:36 and related Surah 12 animal-eating motifs.

topics.headline: plain form keeps horror concrete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ordinary Form I eating makes the scene starkly concrete, with the medial hamza giving the verb an audible catch.
topics.reason: Form and phonetic rows support plain literal consumption and collective-subject agreement.

words.gloss_range: definite collective birds as unified consuming subject
words.root_gloss_range: bird, flight, and omen/fate root; here literal birds acting as agents, with omen pressure retained by the dream-verdict setting
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلطَّيْرُ}} ({{tr:al-ṭayru}}) gives the aftermath an explicit nonhuman subject. The definite collective acts as one consuming force, so the vision is not vague carrion imagery but a scene-specific agent. Spatially, flying creatures descend on the body’s exposed top, making the dream image concrete. The {{ar:ط ي ر}} ({{tr:ṭ-y-r}}) root is narrowed to literal birds, yet omen and fate pressure remains meaningful because these birds are the dream sign becoming the man’s fate, with the fate-bird field visible in 17:13. Other Quranic bird scenes mark life, sign, or ruin (2:260; 3:49; 105:3), while here the heavy onset and collective form make the birds a single death-bearing agent.

topics.headline: definite collective consuming agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the birds are a unified agent in the second branch, not decorative background.
topics.reason: Case, definiteness, and collective agreement make the birds the overt subject of the eating verb.

topics.headline: literal birds carrying omen pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the literal birds are also fate-bearing signs in a dream interpretation, with the fate-bird field visible in 17:13.
topics.reason: Root-family and distribution rows preserve omen pressure while local syntax keeps concrete birds as the referent.

topics.headline: aerial agents attack the exposed apex
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the spatial sharpness of flying agents descending on the body’s exposed top.
topics.reason: Semantic and ordering rows make the postverbal subject land as the agents of the consumption scene.

topics.headline: Quranic bird scenes contrast life and ruin

topics.reason: Intertextual rows compare bird scenes across the Quran without changing the local literal subject.

topics.headline: heavy onset for fate-bearing birds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sound-weight reinforcing the birds’ role as the returning dream image.
topics.reason: Phonetic and echo rows add texture to the concrete bird term.

words.gloss_range: partitive source preposition redirecting eating toward the head as source
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) changes the consumption scene from simple object-eating into source extraction. The birds eat from the head, and that preposition also reverses the earlier dream image in 12:36: what had been above the head becomes material taken from it. Its compact form makes the source relation quick and harsh, and the recitational binding into the following word makes the extraction phrase sound continuous.

topics.headline: source extraction from the head
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition makes the head a source of consumption, not merely an object label.
topics.reason: Grammar and semantic rows select partitive/source relation after the eating verb.

topics.headline: above-head dream becomes from-head fate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the precise prepositional shift from dream placement in 12:36 to interpreted extraction in 12:41.
topics.reason: The row comparing 12:36 with 12:41 makes the governor change a meaningful payoff, while form and sound rows support compactness.

words.gloss_range: possessed head as the condemned man’s exposed source of partitive consumption
words.root_gloss_range: head, summit, chief point, and beginning root; here anatomical head, with apex and identity-bearing pressure retained
words.prose: {{ar:رَأْسِهِ}} ({{tr:raʾsihi}}) keeps the bird image personal: it is his head, the condemned man’s own exposed body part. As the governed source after the preposition, the head is not simply a direct object but the place from which consumption proceeds. The phrase transforms the dream’s above-the-head image in 12:36 into from-the-head consumption in 12:41, so the branch lands not at crucifixion alone but at the exposed apex being eaten. The {{ar:ر أ س}} ({{tr:r-ʾ-s}}) field is locally anatomical, while summit, chief-point, and value-seat pressure make the branch land on the attack against the person’s apex; wider head-punishment and crisis scenes (7:150; 22:19) reinforce that vulnerability without replacing the local image.

topics.headline: his head as source of extraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the image is tied to the specific condemned man through possession and source grammar.
topics.reason: Suffix and prepositional government route the head back to the other prisoner and make it the source of eating.

topics.headline: anatomical head with chief-point pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consumed body part is the person’s apex and identity-bearing point, not a random detail.
topics.reason: Root-range rows preserve summit and chief-point pressure while local context keeps the anatomical head as primary.

topics.headline: dream head-top becomes consumed head-source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the transformation from the dream’s head-top image in 12:36 into the interpretation’s from-head consumption in 12:41.
topics.reason: Same-surah rows connect the rare head root and prepositional change to 12:36.

topics.headline: head as crisis and punishment site
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the head belongs to a wider punishment and crisis imagery field (7:150; 22:19).
topics.reason: Intertextual rows compare head-targeting scenes while leaving this local phrase anatomical and possessed.

topics.headline: death branch lands on exposed head
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the branch ends not at execution but at the exposed head being consumed.
topics.reason: Structure and phonetic rows show the head phrase completing and sharpening the death branch before the decree clause.

words.gloss_range: perfect passive decree/completion verb that seals both future fates as already settled
words.root_gloss_range: deciding, decreeing, completing, and fulfilling root; here passive perfect finality over the whole matter
words.prose: {{ar:قُضِيَ}} ({{tr:quḍiya}}) shifts the ayah from future outcomes to completed finality. The service, crucifixion, and bird-consumption are future in form, but this perfect passive says the matter has already been settled. The {{ar:ق ض ي}} ({{tr:q-ḍ-y}}) root carries decision, completion, and execution of a command; here those senses converge in a formula that gathers both fates under one irreversible decree while suppressing the highest agent. That formula reaches beyond the prison scene to final-resolution language after the flood, at judgment, and in decisive angelic intervention contexts (11:44; 14:22; 6:8). It also turns 12:40’s abstract claim about judgment into a closed personal verdict, with the heavy qaf-dad sound cluster reinforcing the weight of closure.

topics.headline: completed decree before future events
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the time contrast: future fates are enclosed by an already completed decree.
topics.reason: Aspect, voice, and closure-position rows make the passive perfect the totalizing finality verb.

topics.headline: passive hides the decreeing agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human executioner and the higher decreeing agent are both suppressed, but with different effects.
topics.reason: Ellipsis and passive evidence distinguish worldly agent suppression in crucifixion from transcendent finality in the decree clause.

topics.headline: decree, completion, and execution converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb means more than announcement: the affair is decided, completed, and set in motion.
topics.reason: Lexical rows preserve the broad q-d-y range while the local formula narrows it to completed decree over this matter.

topics.headline: cross-surah finality formula in prison

topics.reason: Intertextual rows identify the recurring formula and its final-resolution force across Quranic contexts.

topics.headline: judgment principle becomes personal decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary move from abstract divine judgment in 12:40 into a closed verdict over the prisoners’ petition in 12:41.
topics.reason: Boundary and synthesis rows connect the prior ayah’s judgment claim to the passive formula closing this verdict.

topics.headline: heavy cluster matches irreversible closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the acoustic weight reinforcing the semantic weight of finality.
topics.reason: Phonetic and structure rows support the heavy closure without adding a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: definite abstract matter as the passive subject of the decree
words.root_gloss_range: matter, affair, command, and authority root; here the specific inquiry-matter, with command/decree register active
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَمْرُ}} ({{tr:al-amru}}) names the settled entity: the matter itself is the passive subject of the decree. Its definiteness and following relative clause make it the specific issue the two men sought to have judged, while the abstract singular condenses wine-service, crucifixion, bird-consumption, and petition into one adjudicated affair. The {{ar:أ م ر}} ({{tr:ʾ-m-r}}) root keeps matter and command together, so the prison case feels ordinary and command-laden at once. As the nominal half of the decree formula, it belongs with recurring management and finality language (13:2; 10:3), while the creative command field (2:117; 3:47; 16:40) remains only register pressure. Within Surah 12, the root threads revelation, divine control, human command pressure, and this settled matter (12:15; 12:21; 12:32; 12:41), turning 12:40’s command doctrine into the specific matter now decided.

topics.headline: matter itself is decreed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the matter is not just described after the decree; it is the thing acted upon and settled.
topics.reason: Case and passive-subject evidence make the abstract noun the grammatical patient elevated to subject.

topics.headline: definite singular condenses both fates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that two concrete outcomes are compressed into one specific matter under judgment.
topics.reason: Definiteness, abstraction, and the relative clause identify a single issue already under discussion.

topics.headline: ordinary matter with command pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prisoners’ affair is also heard in the command-and-authority register of the root.
topics.reason: Lexical rows preserve matter and command senses while local grammar selects the specific adjudicated affair.

topics.headline: nominal half of finality formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the noun joins the decree verb to form a recognizable finality and management formula (13:2; 10:3).
topics.reason: Co-occurrence and intertext rows show the q-d-y plus amr pairing across cosmic and judgment contexts.

topics.headline: authority root threads Surah 12
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this matter belongs to a Surah 12 thread of command, authority, and divine control (12:15; 12:21; 12:32; 12:41).
topics.reason: Same-surah and boundary rows link this word to authority scenes at 12:15, 12:21, 12:32, and the prior ayah’s command field.

topics.headline: cosmic command resonance kept secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a cosmic command register (2:117; 3:47; 16:40) without losing the local prison matter.
topics.reason: Creative-command parallels at 2:117, 3:47, and 16:40 are retained as register pressure, not as the direct local sense.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun specifying the decreed matter
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) points back to the singular matter and opens the identifying tail. Its agreement prevents the final clause from floating over the two fates as a plural set; the two outcomes have already been compressed into one matter, and the relative pronoun specifies that very matter as the object of the prisoners’ inquiry.

topics.headline: singular relative points to the matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause identifies the single decreed matter rather than adding a new issue.
topics.reason: Agreement and referential evidence attach the relative clause to the masculine singular matter.

words.gloss_range: preposition-plus-pronoun marking the inquiry domain concerning the decreed matter
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِ}} ({{tr:fīhi}}) packs the domain marker and the pronoun into one form. The phrase means concerning it, but the inside sense still helps: the two men’s question is enclosed within the very matter that has now been decreed. The suffix ties the final petition back to the settled matter and makes the closure a ring rather than a new request.

topics.headline: prepositional pointer to the matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb is routed back to the same matter, not launched as a new action.
topics.reason: Anaphora and prepositional government make the pronoun point to the decreed matter as the inquiry domain.

topics.headline: inside language becomes legal concern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how spatial inside-language becomes juridical concerning-language while still making the petition enclosed within the affair.
topics.reason: Semantic rows narrow the preposition to concern/domain in this context, with spatial pressure retained as local color.

topics.headline: compressed topic and pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compactness of the closure: one short form retrieves the matter and prepares the petition verb.
topics.reason: Form rows show the fused preposition-pronoun compressing reference and domain marking.

words.gloss_range: Form X second-person dual imperfect: you two seek a formal ruling
words.root_gloss_range: youth and fatwa/ruling-request root family; here narrowed to formal petition for interpretation or ruling, with youth-link pressure retained
words.prose: {{ar:تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ}} ({{tr:tastaftiyāni}}) closes the ayah by returning to the two addressees as petitioners. Form X makes them seekers of a ruling, not issuers of it, and the dual ending brings the opening pair back at the final word. The {{ar:ف ت ي}} ({{tr:f-t-y}}) field is narrowed to formal request, while the youth-and-ruling linkage remains pointed in Surah 12 because Joseph the young interpreter is the one they have sought, with the youth/ruling connection already active around 12:30 and 12:36. Most sharply, the present seeking is named only after the perfect passive decree has already sealed the matter. The prison petition also anticipates later court requests for interpretation (12:43; 12:46), while broader authoritative-questioning uses (18:22; 37:149) confirm the formal register; the long dual cadence makes that answered petition the ayah’s final sound.

topics.headline: Form X request for ruling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prisoners are formal petitioners for a ruling, not casual askers about a puzzle.
topics.reason: Form X and local decree context select formal seeking of a ruling.

topics.headline: dual verb returns to opening pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical ring: the ayah opens by calling two men and closes with those two still seeking.
topics.reason: Prefix and dual ending evidence link the final verb back to the same two prison companions.

topics.headline: present petition after completed decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paradoxical order: the decree is grammatically complete before their ongoing petition is named.
topics.reason: Aspect and closure rows contrast the imperfect dual request with the prior perfect passive decree.

topics.headline: petitioners depend on authority outside themselves
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two men do not own the outcome; they request a ruling from outside themselves.
topics.reason: Semantic role and Form X rows make the companions seekers, with the matter routed through the prepositional domain.

topics.headline: youth and ruling root fields converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the formal request word also brushes the Joseph-as-youth field in Surah 12 (12:30; 12:36).
topics.reason: Root-dispute and semantic rows preserve the youth/ruling linkage as pressure, while the local verb means seeking a ruling.

topics.headline: prison petition anticipates court petitions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prison consultation foreshadows later royal and court requests for interpretation (12:43; 12:46).
topics.reason: Same-surah and cross-surah rows place this final verb in a broader authoritative-questioning pattern, especially 12:43 and 12:46.

topics.headline: final long dual cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word gives grammatical and acoustic closure to the answered petition at the ayah’s endpoint.
topics.reason: Phonetic, rarity, and final-position rows support the closing effect.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired construction "one of you ... but the other" joins serving a lord with wine to crucifixion and avian consumption.
baseline_models.mechanism: The doubled allocation distributes the prison companions into opposed transfer regimes: one regains social motion by moving drink to a master, while the other is immobilized and transferred into a scavenging food chain. The contrast is reintegration through service versus exposure through execution.

activation_trace.role: Individual separation supplies the first allocated path and makes the pair distributive rather than generic.
Otherness after a first supplies the ordered complementary path.
Giving drink supplies the first path's literal transfer and restored service relation.
Execution by crucifixion supplies the immobilizing public exposure of the second path.
The prey image turns the exposed person into consumable matter and completes the second transfer.

changed_reading.before: The verse gives two separate predictions, one favorable and one fatal.
changed_reading.after: The verse distributes the pair into opposite exits from prison: one is reabsorbed into a master's service circuit, while the other is immobilized and passed into a scavenging circuit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: "The matter about which you seek a ruling has been decided."
baseline_models.mechanism: Judgment, completion, matter, and requested clarification converge in a speech act of closure. The interpretation does not present itself as a tentative decoding; it claims the force of a settled answer that ends deliberation about these outcomes.

activation_trace.role: Cutting judgment supplies the utterance's decisive rather than conjectural force.
Completion and expiry supply closure of the question as an open process.
Consultation and deliberation supply the process that the settled matter terminates.
Asking for clarification and judgment supplies the interpretive transaction being closed.

changed_reading.before: Joseph reports what will happen after interpreting two dreams.
changed_reading.after: Joseph's report performs closure: it converts a request for interpretation into a settled judgment no longer open to renegotiation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The source dreams supply operations that the focus prediction preserves while replacing their props. Pressing becomes the production side of serving liquid; carrying bread above the head becomes an execution in which the head-bearing person is exposed as food. Interpretation therefore conserves relational structure while transforming object imagery into social and bodily outcomes.

activation_trace.role: Pressure until liquid is expressed supplies the hidden production process behind the first outcome.
A visibly carried load supplies the support relation from which the second outcome is transformed.
Literal elevation fixes the dream food above the dreamer's head and preserves the spatial relation.
Bread supplies the edible object whose consumer relation survives the interpretation.
Serving drink realizes the expressed liquid as a restored social function.
Crucifixion transforms carrying support into the prisoner's own immobilized exposure.
Predation transfers edibility from the overhead bread to the executed person.

structural_cues: 12:36 and 12:41 preserve clause order and repeat the one/other division together with wine, head, eating, and birds.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies paired clauses, pressure, an overhead load, edible bread, and the focus outcomes; I infer that interpretation preserves operators while substituting human endpoints for dream props. A live alternative is simple symbol-to-event correspondence without a general transformation rule.

changed_reading.before: The focus merely states the decoded referents of two dream images.
changed_reading.after: The focus exposes an interpretive transformation: dream operations and spatial relations survive even as their objects become occupational reintegration and bodily execution.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding contrast between dispersed lords and the one overpowering God, followed by the restriction of judgment to God, nests the earthly master in "his lord" beneath a higher adjudicating sovereignty. The passive "has been decided" can therefore carry theological force without erasing the ordinary master-servant sense.

activation_trace.role: Dispersion into parts supplies the fractured plurality of competing lordships.
Divine oneness supplies the singular sovereignty set against that plurality.
Dominance from above supplies the hierarchy under which lesser masters are placed.
Judgment between people supplies the explicit divine jurisdiction echoed by the focus verdict.
Mastery and ownership supply the prisoner's immediate earthly service relation.
Decisive judgment supplies the higher closure governing both allotted outcomes.

structural_cues: The repeated address "companions of the prison" joins 12:39 directly to 12:41, while "lords" becomes the singular possessive "his lord" and "judgment" is followed by passive decision.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the adjacent sovereignty contrast, exclusive divine judgment, an earthly lord, and a passive verdict; I infer a nested authority relation. The live alternative is that the passive only marks prophetic certainty and leaves its agent unstated.

changed_reading.before: "His lord" and "the matter was decided" refer independently to an employer and a firm prediction.
changed_reading.after: The restored servant returns to an earthly master inside, not alongside, the divine jurisdiction that settles both destinies.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah separates the settled dream outcomes from their delayed consequences. One companion escapes, but remembrance fails and Joseph remains confined; closure is exact with respect to what was asked, while the social afterlife of that closure remains vulnerable to memory and time.

activation_trace.role: Escape by separation confirms that one allotted path has taken effect.
Recall after forgetting supplies the human relay on which a later consequence depends.
Loss of remembrance blocks that relay despite fulfillment of the prediction.
Continued dwelling supplies the prolonged consequence that remains open after the verdict.
Completion anchors finality specifically in the matter submitted for interpretation.
Confinement supplies the unchanged condition in which Joseph remains while the outcome unfolds.

structural_cues: 12:42 immediately realizes the survivor branch yet extends Joseph's imprisonment for years through a failed act of remembrance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fulfilled escape, failed memory, and prolonged confinement; I infer that the scope of finality is the submitted outcome rather than every downstream causal path. Alternatively, "decided" may be globally final even though its execution is temporally extended.

changed_reading.before: The closing formula implies that every relevant causal possibility is now immediately finished.
changed_reading.after: The two requested outcomes are fixed, but their consequences unfold through fallible agents and delay; decisiveness is scoped rather than instantaneous.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus body's exposure to birds becomes a small, violent instance of a later conservation contrast: what is left exposed is consumed, while what remains inside a containing form or treasury can survive consumption. The reading links bodily predation to agricultural and administrative depletion without equating those domains.

activation_trace.role: Leaving a thing in place supplies the instruction to retain grain in its protective ear.
Preservation inside an enclosing fort supplies the explicit barrier against consumption.
Securing and storing supplies the administrative endpoint of protected reserves.
Predation supplies the focus case of irreversible consumption of an exposed body.
Flying birds supply the mobile consuming agents that can reach what has been exposed.
The literal head and upper surface locate the body's unprotected point of consumption.

structural_cues: The verb "eat" recurs in 12:43, 12:46, 12:47, and 12:48; the sequence then contrasts grain left in its ear, a fortified remainder, and the treasuries of 12:55.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated consumption plus retention, enclosure, and storage; I infer an exposure-enclosure causal contrast. A live alternative is that repeated eating only carries dream vocabulary and does not generalize into a conservation mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Birds eating from the head is only a gruesome confirmation detail in the second prediction.
changed_reading.after: The exposed head becomes the pericope's first sharp image of unprotected matter entering a consuming system, later countered by enclosure and storage.

context_deltas.mechanism: The decisive prison interpretation becomes an early credential. Later requests return to Joseph, truthful speech is confirmed, truth emerges, and he is entrusted with guarded stores; the focus verdict thus participates in a trajectory from confined answerer to authorized judge and administrator.

activation_trace.role: Truthful speech supplies the explicit reputation attached to the returning request for interpretation.
The uncovering of truth supplies public verification beyond Joseph's own claim.
Establishing and manifesting truth supplies the confirmation that clears the interpreter.
Empowerment supplies the institutional consequence of verified judgment.
Security and trust supply the king's evaluation of Joseph as reliable.
Guarding and watchful care supply the administrative competence finally claimed.
The requested clarification anchors the initial performance by which interpretive competence becomes visible.
Decisive judgment supplies the certainty later tested by fulfillment and public verification.

structural_cues: Requests for fatwa recur in 12:43 and 12:46 before truth, trust, empowerment, and custodianship are explicitly attached to Joseph.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated recourse to Joseph, verified truth, trust, empowerment, and guardianship; I infer that the early accurate verdict functions as a credential in that rise. A live alternative is that exoneration and the famine plan, rather than 12:41 specifically, carry most of the institutional change.

changed_reading.before: The closing declaration serves only the two prisoners' immediate need for certainty.
changed_reading.after: The declaration is also a demonstrable act of judgment whose fulfillment helps move its speaker from confined interpreter toward trusted public authority.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant ف و ت mapping carried for the focus root ف ت ي rather than the ordinary sense of seeking a ruling. The exact focus form and the adjacent closure keep the resonance anchored, but downstream prose should mark it as form-distant and must not present it as the word's translation or etymology.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The request in "the matter about which you seek a ruling" stands after the declaration that the matter is already decided.

activation_trace.role: Preempting an affair without consultation supplies the paradox that the event has outrun the request about it.
Sudden death that forecloses intended action supplies the terminal edge of the second outcome.
Decisive judgment anchors the sense of an inquiry overtaken by settlement.

changed_reading.before: The two companions are simply asking for an interpretation.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, their request is already overtaken by an event that admits no consultation, with one path ending in a death that forecloses further intention.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-ayah activation is surprising because it sets the focus noun "matter" against the later intensive "commanding self" through their shared root. The repeated root, judgment language, and immediate narrative sequence keep it inspectable, but it should be rendered as a contrastive resonance, not as a claim that the two forms have the same local meaning or that settled outcome cancels agency.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: "The matter has been decided" closes an external outcome, while the later sequence describes a self that commands toward harm.

activation_trace.role: Matter and circumstance supply the external object declared settled in the focus.
Cutting judgment supplies closure of that external matter.
Command and compulsion supply the later inward pressure that remains active.
What is held in the inward self locates the continuing command inside the agent.
Badness supplies the harmful direction of the continuing inward command.

changed_reading.before: "The matter" refers only to the predicted events now fixed.
changed_reading.after: The fixed external matter can be heard against an unfixed inner command toward harm, separating closure of outcome from persistence of moral pressure.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant س و ق target for the focus root س ق ي. The serving verb, earthly master, and allocated verdict keep the image attached to the focus, but it should remain a form-distant directional resonance rather than replace the ordinary act of giving drink.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The first companion "will serve his lord wine" within a verdict that assigns each companion a path.

activation_trace.role: Driving and conducting supply an exploratory image of the servant being led back into a royal service track.
Mastery supplies the hierarchy into which that conducted movement returns him.
Decisive allocation supplies the directional force assigning the path.

changed_reading.before: The first companion will resume the isolated task of pouring wine for his master.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the service act also images the companion being conducted back into a master's hierarchy along his allotted route.

strongest_changes: The paired dreams reveal that the focus preserves operations and spatial relations while transforming dream props into occupational and bodily outcomes.
The preceding sovereignty argument nests the earthly master beneath divine judgment and gives the passive verdict a second authority layer.
The following failure of memory bounds the verdict's finality to the submitted outcomes while allowing delayed consequences.
Repeated consumption, enclosure, and storage activate a distinct exposure-versus-preservation reading.
Later truth, trust, empowerment, and guardianship make the prison verdict an early credential for public authority.
summary.what_was_special: The trace retained coexisting social, juridical, temporal, material, and credentialing mechanisms, plus packet-authorized form-distant activations, without merging them into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The passive "has been decided" supports but does not grammatically identify divine agency.
The exposure-enclosure model depends on a reader-supplied causal link across bodily and agricultural consumption domains.
The ف و ت and س و ق outliers are mapped-root resonances, not ordinary morphological claims.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Dream relations become assigned social roles.** س ق ي B001 (giving drink), خ م ر B002, ص ل ب B005 (execution by fastening), ط ي ر B001, and ر ء س B001 preserve the two material structures of 12:36 while converting them into service and exposure. I infer that interpretation crosses from image relation to future office or fate.
2. **The requested answer is now closed as decision.** ق ض ي B001/B004 (decisive ruling; completion) and ف ت ي B004 (clarifying a ruling/answer) make `قضي الأمر` more than prediction. I infer that the interpretive act declares the outcome settled, ending ambiguity for the requesters.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:45 identified the surviving cupbearer as the delayed conduit through which this interpretation reached the court.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Interpretation sealed as an enacted end.** `ق ض ي:B001` is a decisive ruling that settles a matter, and `ق ض ي:B003` is death as an enacted end. The parallel *ammā ... wa-ammā* assigns opposed outcomes, one service and one death, then the passive *quḍiya* closes the matter about which they sought judgment; 12:42 proceeds on the survivor’s path. The packet supplies the bifurcation and closure; I infer that interpretation here commits the dream’s possibilities to distinct temporal endpoints. The final clause reads as performative decisiveness, not a tentative gloss.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:96 restores Jacob's sight and 12:100 identifies the dream's realized outcome; both scenes confirm that an interpretation's force in this surah is finally audited by what comes to pass.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyin başka bir şeyle yakın ve süreğen biçimde birlikte bulunmasını çekirdek anlam olarak verir. Kişi, hayvan, yer ve zamanla kurulan eşlik ilişkisi bu çekirdeğe girerken sahiplik, bir işin başında bulunma ve yanında bir eşlikçi bulunması belirli yapılara bağlı uzantılardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eşlik çekirdeği ile sahiplik, görev ve bir eşlikçisi bulunma gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımları ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şeyle geçici olmayan biçimde birlikte bulunmak, ona eşlik etmek veya onunla yakınlığını sürdürmektir. Belirli yapılarda bir şeyin sahibi ya da sorumlusu olmayı ve kişinin yanında bir eşlikçi bulunmasını da anlatır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, iki tarafın yakın ve süreğen biçimde birlikte bulunması ya da birinin ötekine eşlik etmesidir.
Eşlik eden taraf kişi, hayvan, yer veya zamanla ilişkili olabilir; tekil eşlikçi ve eşlikçiler topluluğu da adlandırılabilir.
Belirli ad tamlamalarında bir şeyin sahibi, ona bağlı kişi veya onun işini yürüten sorumlu kastedilir.
Bir kişinin yanında kendisine eşlik eden birinin bulunması da bu anlam alanının yapıya bağlı uzantısıdır.

يدخل فيه سقي الأرض وحظها من الشرب، الأرض أو الزرع أو النخل المسقي، الساقية والنهير، والمساقاة في النخيل والكروم.
يدخل فيه السقاء والقربة والجلد المتخذ سقاء، والسقاية موضع الشراب أو البيت المجتمع للماء أو صواع الملك، والمسقاة لما تعلق عليه الجرار والأكواز.
يدخل فيه السقي بمعنى الماء الأصفر أو النفافيخ في شحم البطن، سقى بطنه، الاستسقاء، وماء المشيمة الخارج على رأس الولد.
يدخل فيه قول سقاه الله، سقاه الله الغيث، اللهم أسقنا، واستعمال السقيا في الدعاء أو التمني بالماء والغيث.
يدخل فيه السقي على فعيل بمعنى السحابة العظيمة القطر الشديدة الوقع.
يدخل فيه السقي بمعنى البردي أو القصب الناعم الذي لا يفوته الماء، وما يشبه به من أنبوب السقي.
يدخل فيه سقي الثوب من العصفر ونحوه إذا صبغ وأشرب اللون.
يدخل فيه سقى على فلان بما يكره وكرر عليه ما يكرهه، وسقي قلبه بالعداوة تسقية.
يدخل فيه أسقى الرجل أو سقى زيد عمرا عند من فسره بالاغتياب والغيبة الخبيثة.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الرب بمعنى الله تعالى، ومالك الشيء، وسيده المطاع، وصاحبه، ورب الدار والدابة والملك
branches.source_phrase_ar: الرب: الله تبارك وتعالى؛ ورب كل شيء مالكه (jamhara); رب كل شئ: مالكه؛ وقد قالوه في الجاهلية للملك؛ رببت القوم: سستهم (sihah); يكون الرب: المالك؛ ويكون الرب: السيد المطاع؛ ويكون الرب: المصلح (tahdhib); الرب مصدر مستعار للفاعل؛ لا يقال الرب مطلقا إلا لله؛ رب الدار ورب الفرس (mufradat); فالرب المالك والخالق والصاحب؛ والله جل ثناؤه الرب (maqayis)

يدخل فيه الربة والجماعات الكثيرة، والربيون إذا فسروا بالألوف أو الجماعات، ورباب القبائل لاجتماعهم
يدخل فيه الربيب والربيبة للولد المربوب من زوج سابق، والراب والرابة لمن يقوم على أمره، والحاضنة

يدخل فيه الربابة للجلدة أو الوعاء الذي تجمع فيه القداح أو سهام الميسر، وجماعة السهام نفسها
يدخل فيه الربابة والرباب للعهد والميثاق والجوار، والأربة للمعاهدين، والرباب للعشور إذا جعل كالعهد

يدخل فيه الربب للماء الكثير، ويقال للعذب، من جهة اجتماع الماء
يدخل فيه الربرب لقطيع بقر الوحش، وقيل لجماعة البقر أو الإبل

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ربا الشيء إذا زاد أو ارتفع، وربت الأرض إذا انتفخت وزادت، والرابي الزائد أو العالي، وأربى عليه إذا أشرف أو زاد عليه.
يدخل فيه الربوة والرابية والرباوة والرباة وما ارتفع من الأرض، مع اختلاف لغات الكلمة.
يدخل فيه الربا في البيع أو القرض، والزيادة على رأس المال، والربية لغة أو اسم خاص للربا.
يدخل فيه الربو بمعنى النفس العالي أو البهر أو الانبهار، وما يصيب الإنسان أو الدابة من علو النفس أو الانتفاخ من مشي أو عدو أو فزع.
يدخل فيه ربيت الولد أو تربيته بمعنى غذوته، وربا الولد أو الزرع بالنماء، وربوت أو ربيت في القوم بمعنى نشأت فيهم.
يدخل فيه الأربية أو الأربيتان بمعنى أصل الفخذ أو لحمتين ناتئتين في أصول الفخذين من باطن.
يدخل فيه قولهم جاء في أربية قومه أي في أهل بيته من بني الأعمام ونحوهم.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sarhoş eden bilinen içkiyi, onun bekleyip olgunlaşmasını ve aklı kaplamasını aynı dalda toplar. Bununla birlikte içkinin kapsamı bütün sarhoş ediciler ile üzüm veya hurmadan yapılan türler arasında farklı aktarılmıştır; tanım bu kapsam ayrılığını tek ve dar bir madde tanımına indirgemez.

lexicalization_scope.note: İçki adı çekirdekte tutulur; olgunlaşma, yapım, satış, sürekli içme, hayvana içirme ve sonrasında kalan sersemlik yalnızca kendi biçimlerinde geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Aklı örten ve sarhoşluk veren içki ile bu içkinin bekleme sonucu olgunlaşıp kaynaması veya kokusunun değişmesi alanıdır. Kapsamı bütün sarhoş edici içkiler olarak da, üzüm ya da hurmadan yapılan türlerle sınırlı olarak da aktarılır; yapıcısı, satıcısı, içeni ve etkisinin kalıntısı ayrı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: İçilince aklı etkileyip sarhoşluk veren bilinen içkidir.
İçkinin kapsamı bütün sarhoş edicileri içine alan geniş yorum ile üzüm veya hurma kökenli türlere bağlanan dar yorum arasında değişir.
İçkinin bekleyerek olgunlaşması, kaynaması veya kokusunun değişmesi üretim sürecini bildirir.
İçkiyi yapan veya satan kişi, sürekli içen kimse ve sarhoşluğun ardından kalan sersemlik bu alana bağlı adlandırmalardır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sarhoş eden bilinen içkiyi ve onun olgunlaşmasını ortak çekirdekte birleştirir; içkinin madde kapsamı geniş ve dar yorumlarla, kişi ve artçı etki adları ise bağlı kullanımlarla verilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: İçkiyi merkez alırken onun bekleyip kaynama veya koku değişimiyle olgunlaşmasını da açıkça kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Hem sarhoş edici içkiyi hem de içkinin olgunlaşma sürecini korur.

concept_map.definition: Besini ağız yoluyla tüketme eylemi ve bu eylemin doğrudan çevresindeki yiyecek, tek yeme, çok yiyen kişi, birlikte yiyen kişi ve başkasını doyuran kişi rolleridir.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, yiyeceği tüketme eylemidir.
Yenen şey, bir yeme keresi veya tek lokma da aynı anlam çevresinde adlandırılır.
Çok yiyen, birlikte yiyen ve başkasını doyuran kişiler eyleme katılım biçimlerine göre adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak anlatımı, yeme eylemini temel alır ve yiyecek, tek lokma ya da yeme, çok yiyen, yemeğe eşlik eden ve doyuran kişi adlarını bu temel etrafında birleştirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Eylem ile ona doğrudan bağlı nesne, kerelik ve kişi rollerinin birlikte anlatıldığı genel kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yeme çekirdeğini, yiyeceği, tek kereliği ve katılımcı rollerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin besini tüketmesi anlatıldığında doğal eylem karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Besini tüketme eylemini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kimseyle aynı öğünde birlikte yiyen kişi için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Birlikte yeme ilişkisini ve kişi rolünü korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir öğünlük yeme veya tek lokma

error_profile.preserves: Bir şeyi kullanıp bitirme yönünü korur.
error_profile.adds: Besin dışındaki her türlü nesnenin harcanması veya yok edilmesi anlamını ekler.
error_profile.collision: Yemeye özgü çekirdeği genel tüketimle karıştırır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أكل العرض، الغيبة، أكل لحوم الناس، وذو أكلة أو إكلة في الناس.
يدخل فيه آكلت بين القوم، الإيكال بين الناس، والمؤكل بمعنى النمام أو من يحرش ويفسد.
يدخل فيه أكلتني أو آكلتني ما لم آكل بمعنى ادعيته علي، وآكلتك فلانا بمعنى أمكنته منه.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kanatlı canlıyı ve uçma eylemini merkeze alırken hafiflik, hız, uçurma, kuş desenli kumaş ve kuşu bol yer gibi açıkça belirtilen kullanımları da aynı dalda toplar. Verilen çerçeve bu çekirdek ile ona bağlı kullanımları doğru biçimde yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın kuş ve uçuş biçimleriyle bunlardan türeyen at, kumaş ve yer birlikteliklerini ayırır; özel birliktelikleri yalın kök anlamına genellemez.

concept_map.definition: Kanatlı bir canlının havada ilerlemesi ve bu hareketi yapan canlıdır. Hafifçe ya da çok hızlı gitme, bir şeyi uçurma, hızlı ve atılgan at, kuş desenli kumaş ve kuşu bol yer kullanımları bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Kanatlı canlı ve onun havada ilerleme hareketi dalın ortak çekirdeğidir.
Hafifçe veya olağanüstü hızlı ilerleme, uçuş hareketine benzetilerek anlatılır.
Bir canlıyı ya da nesneyi havalanmaya yöneltme, uçuşun ettirgen biçimidir.
At için kullanılan özel birliktelik hız ve yürek pekliğini bildirir.
Kumaştaki kuş resimleri ile bir yerdeki kuş bolluğu, kuşa bağlı niteleme kullanımlarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların toplu anlatımı kuşu, uçuşu ve uçurmayı temel alır; hız benzetmesini, hızlı atı, kuş desenli dokumayı ve kuşu bol araziyi de buna bağlı kullanımlar olarak verir.

error_profile.preserves: Kanatlı canlıyı ve onun havada ilerleme hareketini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gerçek uçuşta ve uçuşa benzetilen çok hızlı ilerlemede kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Havada ilerleme ile hız benzetmesini bağlama göre korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyi ya da canlıyı uçmaya yöneltme bağlamına uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Uçuş hareketinin ettirgen katılımcı düzenini açıkça korur.

Altı dal, yalın biçimler ile yalnızca belirli söz birlikteliklerinde yaşayan anlamları birlikte barındırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ibare, insanın ve başka varlıkların başını temel alır ve buradan bir şeyin en üst bölümüne uzanır. Sarımsağın bütün birimi, başın büyüklüğü veya rengi, baş yaralanması, başların alınması ya da satılması ve baş önde çıkma gibi kullanımlar bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır; önderlik ve kılıç kabzası bu dalın parçası değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak baş ve üst bölüm anlamı, yalnız belirli yapılarda görülen sayma, niteleme, yaralama, alma, satma ve çıkma kullanımlarından ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın ya da başka bir varlığın başı ile bir şeyin en üst bölümüdür. Bu temel, bir bütünü baş olarak sayma; başın büyüklük, renk veya yaralanma durumunu niteleme; başları alma ya da satma ve baş önde çıkma gibi bağlı kullanımlara uzanır.

facets.statement: İnsanın veya başka bir varlığın başını ve bir şeyin en üst bölümünü belirtir.
Sarımsak gibi tek bir bütün oluşturan bir ürünü baş birimiyle sayar.
Başın olağandan büyük olması, renginin ayırt edici olması veya bedensel durumun yalnız başta kalması gibi nitelikleri bildirir.
Başa vurmayı ve bunun sonucunda başın yaralanmış olmasını anlatır.
Hayvan başlarını alma veya kesilmiş başları satma işini baş nesnesi üzerinden adlandırır.
Bir yerden başını öne vererek çıkma biçimini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, başı ve bir şeyin en üst bölümünü ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Aynı toplu tanıklık sarımsağın baş olarak sayılmasını, başın büyüklük ve renk özelliklerini, baş yaralanmasını, başlara yönelen alma ve satma işlerini ve baş önde çıkmayı bu çekirdeğe bağlı kullanımlar olarak bir araya getirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: İnsan veya başka bir varlığın başı ile bir nesnenin en üst bölümünü karşılayan temel anlam için uygundur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı yasaklamanın karşıtı olan yapma isteği, yükümlü kılma ve bu isteğin söz kalıbı olarak tanımlar. Geçici çerçeve çıplak ve yapı içi kullanımları birlikte tutar, fakat anlamı genel konuya veya yöneticiliğe genişletmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik tür mixed_non_bare olduğu için çıplak buyruk anlamı ile özel kalıp kullanımları ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Birine belirli bir eylemi yapmasını bildiren ve onu o eylemle yükümlü kılan söz ya da isteme eylemi.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, yasaklamanın karşıtı olan yapma isteği ve yükümlü kılmadır.
Bazı biçimler bu isteğin söz dizisindeki kullanımını veya bir kez uyulacak özel yükümlülüğü gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ortak olarak bu anlamı yasaklamanın karşıtı olan eylem buyurma ve birini bir şeyi yapmakla yükümlü kılma alanında toplar.

error_profile.loses: Yükümlülüğün resmi veya bağlayıcı gücünü zayıflatabilir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الأمر المضاد للنهي، والتكليف بالفعل، وصيغ الطلب مثل مر وأمر، وامتثال الأمر.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الأمر الذي هو نقيض النهي قولك افعل كذا (maqayis)؛ الأمر نقيض النهي وإذا أمرت من الأمر قلت اؤمر (ayn)؛ أمرته بكذا أمرا والجمع الأوامر (sihah)؛ الأمر معروف نقيض النهي (tahdhib)؛ مصدر أمرته إذا كلفته أن يفعل شيئا، والتقدم بالشيء (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الإمرة والإمارة والولاية، والأمير والمؤمر، وتولية شخص أميرا أو تسلطه.
يدخل فيه الكثرة والنماء والبركة واليمن، وكثرة المال أو القوم أو النسل.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi başkasıyla danışmayı, topluluğun kendi arasında görüş alışverişini, kişinin kendi içinde tartıp karar bağlamasını ve görüş kabulünü birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve bu danışma ve karar oluşturma alanını doğru yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik tür mixed_non_bare olduğu için karşılıklı danışma, kendi içinde tartma ve görüş kabulü ayrı tutulur.

Kişinin kendi içinde farklı eğilimleri tartıp bir görüşe bağlaması özel bir kullanımdır.
Görüşü kabul etme veya karar haline getirme anlamı danışma sürecinin sonucuna uzanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı danışma, karşılıklı görüş alışverişi, kişinin kendi içinde düşünmesi ve sonunda görüşü kabul edip karara bağlaması alanında toplar.

branches.source_phrase_ar: فلان يؤامر نفسيه أي نفس تأمره بشيء ونفس تأمره بآخر (maqayis)؛ آمرته في أمري إذا شاورته، والائتمار والاستئمار المشاورة وكذلك التآمر (sihah)؛ ائتمر القوم إذا تشاوروا، أي كيف يرتئي رأيا ويشاور نفسه ويعقد عليه (tahdhib)؛ الائتمار قبول الأمر، ويقال للتشاور ائتمار (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الإمر أو الإمرة للرجل الضعيف الرأي أو الأحمق الذي يستأمر كل أحد ويأتمر لكل أمر.
يدخل فيه الإمر لولد الضأن أو الخروف، والإمرة للأنثى أو الرخل.
يدخل فيه الأمر بمعنى الإبداع والإنشاء المختص بالله، والتعبير عن سرعة الإيجاد بالقول.
يدخل فيه السنان المؤمر أي المحدد، وأمر القناة بمعنى جعل سنان فيها.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök birbiriyle karışabilen ama ayrı duran birçok alan taşır: konu ve hal, buyruk, yönetim yetkisi, bereketli çoğalma, belirti, ağır yadırganan olay, danışma, zayıf görüşlü kişi, koyun yavrusu, Tanrı'ya özgü yaratma ve mızrağa uç takma. identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi güçlük çıkaran yargı kurallarını açıklama ve bunlara cevap verme çekirdeğini; cevap isteyen kişiyi, düş yorumunu ve bir bilene başvurarak aralarında yargılaşanları ayrı kullanımlar olarak açıkça içerir. Verilen çerçeve bu katmanları aynı çekirdeğe bağlı tutar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yargı sorusuna açıklayıcı cevap verme çekirdeğini korur; soru isteme, düş yorumlama ve topluca bir bilene başvurma gibi türemiş kullanımları bu çekirdekten ayrı gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Bilgili bir kişinin güçlük doğuran bir yargı kuralını açıklaması veya bu konudaki soruya cevap vermesidir; karşı katılımcı bu açıklamayı isteyen kişidir. Düş yorumlamak bu cevaplama modelinin bir uzantısı, bir bilene topluca başvurup aralarında yargılaşmak ise ona bağlı özel bir toplumsal kullanımdır.

facets.statement: Güçlük doğuran bir yargı kuralı bilgili kişi tarafından açıklanır ve ona ilişkin soruya cevap verilir.
Açıklamayı isteyen kişi hükmü sorar; bilgili kişi de sorulan mesele hakkında açıklayıcı cevabı üretir.
Bir kişinin gördüğü düşü ona yorumlamak, açıklayıcı cevap verme düzeninin özel bir uzantısıdır.
İnsanların bir bilene başvurup aralarındaki uyuşmazlığı onun önüne götürmeleri, cevap ve karar arayışına bağlı toplu bir kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği, güç bir yargı sorununu açıklama ve sorana cevap vermedir. Soru isteme bunun karşı katılımcı yönüdür; bazı kaynaklar ayrıca düş yorumlamayı açıklama modelinin uzantısı, topluca bir bilene başvurmayı ise uyuşmazlıkla ilgili özel kullanım olarak verir.
